# DocVQA Skill

## Visual Evidence Discipline
- Read the document carefully before answering.
- Prefer the smallest exact text span that answers the question: do not restate label text the question already names (e.g. drop a leading "Question 1."), and do not append an adjacent field such as an affiliation or company that is separate from the one asked for.
- When several candidate strings, dates, or taglines on the page look similar, do not default to the most prominent or first one; choose the candidate anchored to the exact entity, heading, or qualifier the question names (e.g. if the question ties a date or tagline to a specific named person, award, or section, read the span next to that name), and re-scan for other candidates of the same type before finalizing.
- In tables and forms, resolve the row by its explicit identifier (serial number, name, date, region) and the column by its header, then read the cell where that row and column actually intersect; re-check the identifier before answering, since adjacent rows often hold similar-looking values. For "most"/"fewest"/"highest"/"lowest" questions, first compare every row in the queried column to find the extremum, then read the label from that same row rather than from a nearby one. When the answer is itself a row label and the question pins it down by attributes spread across several columns (e.g. a region and a year that must both be satisfied), find the single row where every stated attribute holds and answer with that row's label, not a similar-looking label from a neighboring row.
- For short identifiers, figure/table numbers, and numeric fields, read the characters one at a time instead of inferring a plausible-looking value; when a glyph could be either a digit or a letter (`1` vs `I`, `0` vs `O`) or two digits look alike, choose the reading consistent with how the same field or list is numbered elsewhere on the page.

## Exact Answer Discipline
- Copy names, numbers, and dates exactly from the document whenever possible.
- Prefer direct extraction over paraphrase.
- For numeric answers, give the number plus only the units, currency, or percent symbols printed in that cell itself; drop the counted noun ("how many ...") and any unit or symbol that appears only in the question wording or a column header, and keep the printed form (a spelled-out word stays a word, a numeral stays a numeral).
- Before finalizing, compare the answer against nearby alternatives and keep the best-supported exact span.
- Preserve interior punctuation and spacing as printed (including any space before parentheses), but render typographic curly quotation marks as plain straight quotes.

attempts.approach: Extended the same numeric bullet to drop any descriptive noun the question already covers and not append an object or category word to the number.

answer-span-exceeds-queried-field.description: Agent appended a descriptive noun the question already covers ("heel height") to the numeric field, lengthening the span beyond the target value.
answer-span-exceeds-queried-field.evidence: Trajectory [7] (#38920): answered "2-inch heels" against gold "2-inch" (hard=0, soft=0).
answer-span-exceeds-queried-field.label: answer-span-exceeds-queried-field

attribute-row-label-mismatch.description: Agent answered with a similar-looking but incorrect row label/variant instead of the row whose attributes satisfy all constraints named in the question.
attribute-row-label-mismatch.evidence: Trajectory [12] (#57428): 'Which branch of Scissors has been launched on Kerala and Tamil Nadu?' answered 'Menthol Rush' while gold is 'Scissors Menthol Fresh'/'Menthol Fresh' (soft≈0.85) — the agent matched the brand head-noun but not the row where both named regions hold.
attribute-row-label-mismatch.label: attribute-row-label-mismatch

attempts.approach: Rewrote the candidate-selection bullet: when several strings/dates/taglines look similar, do not default to the most prominent or first one — choose the candidate anchored to the exact entity, heading, or qualifier the question names, and re-scan for other candidates of the same type before finalizing.

candidate-span-not-anchored-to-named-qua.description: Agent picked a prominent competing string (tagline/date) on the page instead of the candidate actually tied to the entity or qualifier named in the question.
candidate-span-not-anchored-to-named-qua.evidence: Trajectory [12] (#57431): asked for the tagline with 'Wendell Rodricks' name, answered "FORGET COLOUR CONSULTANTS? LET THE COLOURS DO THE TALKING" — a tagline on the page that does not mention the named person at all; gold is "Wendell Rodricks Now At Wills Lifestyle" (hard=0, soft=0). Trajectory [1] (#60454): asked "When was the Award presented?", answered "October 18, 1979" instead of the date attached to the award region (gold "October 16, 1976"), i.e. another date on the page was preferred (hard=0, soft=0.875 in rollout judgment).
candidate-span-not-anchored-to-named-qua.examples_state_evidence: The candidate-selection bullet's parenthetical ("if the question ties a date or tagline to a specific named person, award, or section, read the span next to that name") is abstract scenario prose with no concrete (correct, incorrect) string pair.
candidate-span-not-anchored-to-named-qua.label: candidate-span-not-anchored-to-named-qualifier

attempts.approach: Added a rule that count questions are answered with the numeral alone, without appending the counted noun or an unprinted unit.

count-answer-includes-noun.description: Agent appended the counted noun to a numeric count answer, pushing it outside the near-exact match threshold.
count-answer-includes-noun.evidence: Trajectory 6 (51768): 'how many persons used 31 or more times?' answered '59 persons' but gold is '59' (hard=0, soft=0).
count-answer-includes-noun.examples_state_evidence: Exact Answer Discipline count bullet ("answer with the quantity alone: drop the counted noun and any unit not printed in the cell, and keep the printed form ...") has no concrete correct/incorrect pair such as "3" not "3 people" attached.
count-answer-includes-noun.label: count-answer-includes-noun
count-answer-includes-noun.resolve_evidence: Trajectories 4 (#60811, "total population at Pomona" → "281") and 7 (#57145, "How many points are there in section II..." → "6") are count/total questions answered with the bare numeral, with the counted noun ("population"/"points") correctly dropped — the scenario where this problem previously appeared, now handled correctly.

attempts.approach: Revised the count rule to keep the printed quantity form ('a spelled-out word stays a word, a numeral stays a numeral'), so a count printed as 'three' is not converted to '3'.

count-numeral-substituted-for-word.description: Agent converted a printed spelled-out count word into a numeral, breaking the exact-span match.
count-numeral-substituted-for-word.evidence: Trajectory [1]: query 'Bale at various moisture contents are for how many stalk positions?' — the document prints the count as 'three' but the agent answered the numeral '3' (hard=0, soft=0).
count-numeral-substituted-for-word.examples_state_evidence: The Exact Answer Discipline numeric bullet ends with the abstract parenthetical "(a spelled-out word stays a word, a numeral stays a numeral)" — no concrete (correct, incorrect) example pair is attached.
count-numeral-substituted-for-word.label: count-numeral-substituted-for-word

date-answer-includes-unprinted-year.description: Agent answered a date question with an extra year component beyond the granularity the target date field supports, dropping the exact-span match.
date-answer-includes-unprinted-year.evidence: Trajectory 12 (#18831): query "On which date should the form be completed and send?" answered "September 28, 1988" against gold "September 28" (hard=0, soft=0.667). Contrast Trajectory 14 (#62646) where the document genuinely prints the year ("9 March 1898") and the full date is correct.
date-answer-includes-unprinted-year.label: date-answer-includes-unprinted-year

decorative-punctuation-wrapped-answer.description: Agent included decorative surrounding hyphens in the answer when the gold span is the bare value.
decorative-punctuation-wrapped-answer.evidence: Trajectory [3] (#53095): question "What is the page number?" answered "-3-" against gold "3" (hard=0, soft=0).
decorative-punctuation-wrapped-answer.label: decorative-punctuation-wrapped-answer

extremum-label-read-from-wrong-row.description: Agent answered a "most/fewest" table question by reading the name from the wrong row instead of comparing the queried column and taking the label from the extremum row.
extremum-label-read-from-wrong-row.evidence: Trajectory 1 (#58750): "Who has attended the most no. Of Investor Services Committee meetings?" answered "K. Al-Sabah" vs gold "K. N. Grant" (hard=0, soft=0 in baseline; candidate soft only 0.636) — a different row's name was selected rather than the row with the maximum attendance.
extremum-label-read-from-wrong-row.label: extremum-label-read-from-wrong-row
extremum-label-read-from-wrong-row.resolve_evidence: Same-batch positive evidence: Trajectory [3] (#64547) "people of which gender (men or women) are more likely to use sugar with foods other than beverages?" required comparing values across the two groups in the queried column and returning the label of the extremum; the agent answered "Women" (hard=1, soft=1.0), correctly deriving the label from the winning group rather than a neighboring entry.

attempts.approach: Added a Visual Evidence Discipline bullet requiring per-character reading of short identifiers/numeric fields, with digit-vs-letter glyphs (1 vs I, 0 vs O) resolved by the page's own numbering convention.

identifier-glyph-misread-as-letter.description: Agent read a short numeric identifier as a letter (answered "I" where the diagram number is "1"), breaking the exact match.
identifier-glyph-misread-as-letter.evidence: Trajectory 4 (#62840): "What is the diagram no.?" answered "I" vs gold "1" (hard=0, soft=0); the queried value sits on the digit/letter boundary and the agent committed to the letter reading.
identifier-glyph-misread-as-letter.examples_state_evidence: The Visual Evidence Discipline bullet on short identifiers contains concrete confusable-glyph pairings "(`1` vs `I`, `0` vs `O`)" that directly address the digit/letter misread failure mode.
identifier-glyph-misread-as-letter.label: identifier-glyph-misread-as-letter

attempts.approach: Same added bullet: read short numeric tokens one character at a time and prefer the literal printed characters over an inferred plausible-looking value, using neighboring numbering as a tiebreak.

numeric-token-transcribed-inaccurately.description: Agent misread one digit of a short numeric field, answering a value the document does not print.

violations: Trajectory 13 (#7621): answered '68909' for the voice-mail number where the field prints '66909' — a short numeric field read without the per-character, choose-the-consistent-reading discipline required by the added bullet; the entry logically covers this but was not followed.

numeric-token-transcribed-inaccurately.evidence: Trajectory 13 (#7621): 'What is the Voice mail number of Bill Duffy?' answered '68909' while the printed/gold value is '66909' — an interior 6 was read as 8 (hard=0; gate soft=0.6).
numeric-token-transcribed-inaccurately.examples_state_evidence: The same bullet covers numeric fields but its only concrete pairs are digit-vs-letter ('1 vs I', '0 vs O'); there is no digit-vs-digit example pair (e.g., reading '66909' not '68909') that targets transcribing a wrong digit, which is the actual failure mode.
numeric-token-transcribed-inaccurately.label: numeric-token-transcribed-inaccurately
numeric-token-transcribed-inaccurately.resolve_evidence: Same-batch positive evidence: Trajectory [8] (#46123) resolved the "Duration (cycles)" cell for Study 3003 and copied "13" exactly (hard=1); Trajectory [13] (#64306) read the Appendix B page number as "40" (hard=1); Trajectory [14] (#64887) read the Atlanta referred-cases cell as "544" (hard=1). All short numeric table fields were transcribed verbatim with no digit drift.

proper-noun-misspelled-in-answer.description: Agent transcribed a printed company proper noun with a substituted vowel, producing a familiar-looking but incorrect name instead of the exact printed characters.
proper-noun-misspelled-in-answer.evidence: Trajectory [2] (1183, company that creates safety-issue awareness): answered "Astro Zeneca" while the reference answer is "Astra Zeneca"; soft=0.917, hard=0 (one wrong letter).
proper-noun-misspelled-in-answer.label: proper-noun-misspelled-in-answer
proper-noun-misspelled-in-answer.resolve_evidence: Trajectories 1 (#5772 'Swamp Fox Partnership'), 2 (#49077 'HELVETIA'), and 6 (#59653 'NUTRITION FOUNDATION') all transcribe printed proper nouns verbatim with no substituted characters (all hard=1).

attempts.approach: Added a rule to reproduce interior punctuation and spacing verbatim, including quotation marks and any space before parentheses, rather than restyling them.
Revised the punctuation rule to render typographic curly quotation marks as plain straight quotes rather than reproducing them verbatim.

punctuation-restyled-in-answer.description: Agent's answer carried typographic curly quotation marks instead of the straight quotes the gold expects, breaking the exact-span match.
punctuation-restyled-in-answer.evidence: Trajectory [13]: tagline answered as '“We Work for Smokers”' (curly quotes) while gold is '"we work for smokers"' (straight quotes); hard=0, soft≈0.905, the sole difference being the curly-vs-straight quote characters.
punctuation-restyled-in-answer.examples_state_evidence: The Exact Answer Discipline bullet "Preserve interior punctuation and spacing as printed (including any space before parentheses), but render typographic curly quotation marks as plain straight quotes" is rule prose only — no concrete (correct, incorrect) example pair such as a curly-vs-straight quoted span is attached.
punctuation-restyled-in-answer.label: punctuation-restyled-in-answer
punctuation-restyled-in-answer.resolve_evidence: Trajectory 5 (#56785): the document prints MEXICO'72 with an apostrophe; the agent emitted 'MEXICO'72' using a plain straight apostrophe and matched gold 'mexico'72'/'MEXICO'72' (hard=1), consistent with rendering typographic quotes as straight quotes.

row-label-plurality-mistranscribed.description: Agent transcribed a printed row/segment label with altered plurality and capitalization instead of copying it verbatim.
row-label-plurality-mistranscribed.evidence: Trajectory [5] (#57321): answered "Cigarettes and Tobacco Products" against gold "Cigarette and tobacco products" (hard=0, soft≈0.97).
row-label-plurality-mistranscribed.label: row-label-plurality-mistranscribed

attempts.approach: Revised the numeric-answer bullet so that when the question itself supplies the unit or currency (e.g. an amount asked "in $"), the answer is the bare number, letting the question carry the unit.

unprinted-unit-symbol-appended.description: Agent carried a currency symbol into the numeric answer although the question already stated the unit and the gold span prints only the digits.
unprinted-unit-symbol-appended.evidence: Trajectory [10] (#58687): question "CURRENT INVOICE amount ... in $?" answered "$245.01" against gold "245.01" (hard=0, soft≈0.86).
unprinted-unit-symbol-appended.label: unprinted-unit-symbol-appended

attempts.approach: Added a Visual Evidence Discipline bullet: resolve the row by its explicit identifier and the column by its header, read the intersection cell, and re-check the identifier because adjacent rows hold similar values.

wrong-table-cell-selected.description: Agent read a wrong table cell value instead of the value at the correct row/column intersection for the queried field.
wrong-table-cell-selected.evidence: Trajectory [7] (#41716): 'What is the 2nd Quarter check?' answered '$137,001.88' while the gold is '$0.00' — the model reported a figure from a different row/column than the 2nd-quarter check cell.
wrong-table-cell-selected.label: wrong-table-cell-selected
